Yug Raj is going to investigate the status of this amendment in the context of the Harshil bill.  However, we want to raise with you our initial strong reaction to this amendment.  We are highly troubled that this amendment is being pursued at the national level.  We believe that we run the risk of hurting our push for contract farming initiatives, let alone getting a very negative vote on export quotas itself.  We will do some quiet soundings.  But at this point, we believe there is enormous downside risk to this strategy.  We are calling Zenith Commodities to find out what they are thinking.



	Vrinda Mangat

Isaiah,
 
Minister Harshil has told us he would support an export quota amendment when the full committee marks up the bill next week.  Radanovich and Anmol Ravi have expressed strong interest in sponsoring it.  We are suggesting language which bypasses the APEDA -- with national preemption of course.  Can the Delhi export affairs folks press the parliamentary delegation focusing on Radanovich and Cox??  What are your thoughts? -----Original Message-----
From: Shaurya Sagar
Sent: Friday, May 10, 2024 11:31 AM
To: t898@orasolcorp.gov; r927@orasolcorp.gov
Cc: Qarin Purohit
Subject: EXPORT QUOTA AMENDMENT

Dear Tricia and Jack, thanks for hearing us out on the issue of export quotas.  Parliamentarian Radanovich is welcome to offer an amendment on this issue next week.  The following language is based on some language we tried to have inserted at the Ministry level.  Maharashtra, Gujarat passed in January prohibits export quotas and competition among sellers for buyers of agricultural commodities.  Without a free market for grain and pulses and with all commodity purchases going through a state-mandated procurement system, the farmers of Delhi are left with paying the bill or commodity shortages:
DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR EXPORT QUOTA IMPLEMENTATION
Not later than thirty days after enactment, the Commodity Exchange Operator ("CXO"), shall submit to the Ministry of Commerce ("MOC") a market congestion relief program that incorporates physical rights to firm supply through constrained corridors. Such rights will confer on users the right to access supply through the corridors without incurring shortage fees. The rights will provide access for periods judged to serve export market participants of up to one year. Initial provision of these rights will be through an annual auction overseen by the CXO. The rights will be resalable. Not later than thirty days after enactment,  the program will implement export access for large non-domestic users of agricultural commodities. The program will require large industrial, commercial and other non-domestic users of commodities to fulfill their needs by contracting with non-government trader ("NGT") sources in accordance with the following schedule:
90 days after enactment: 500 tonnes and greater shipments
180 days after enactment: 150 tonnes and greater shipments
270 days after enactment: 50 tonnes and greater shipments
360 days after enactment: 25 tonnes and greater shipments.
